properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-21: the near-match guard's floor lands inside a dense near-tie and then takes 3 of it — 9 nodes cleared the floor, 3 were shown, and ranks 4 and 5 were 0.006 apart, so which near-duplicate a caller sees is decided by score noise rather than by relevance
properties.statement:
WHAT WAS OBSERVED. On 2026-09-21 an idea was captured (`dec:idea-may-a-caller-asserted-identity-be-trusted-and-for-what`) that substantially duplicates an idea open here since 2026-08-26 (`dec:idea-authentication-is-somebody-elses-layer-and-the-line-is-the-contributor-id`). `add_decision` returned no near-match block at all. Minutes earlier on the same design `add_requirement` had returned one and `add_capability` had hard-REFUSED a write, so the guard was working.

THE MEASUREMENT. `search_design` was re-run with the same text the guard searches on (`name` + the decision body as written), window 12, replicating `search_first`:

    self (the new node)                              474.76
    floor = self x NEAR_MATCH_RATIO (0.5)           ~237.4
    2. the-change-ledger-records-what-moved-never-who 260.25   shown
    3. the-hosted-surface-is-read-only                257.90   shown
    4. authentication-is-somebody-elses-layer         245.19   NOT SHOWN
    5. a-session-holds-several-graphs                 245.18
    ...
    11. the-loop-says-what-is-owed-to-a-person        235.48   below floor

NINE non-self hits clear the floor. `NEAR_MATCH_LIMIT` is 3.

⭐ THE CAUSE, and it is not the threshold. Two constants interact badly at scale. The floor is RELATIVE to the new node's own score, and a node scored against its own text sits structurally far above everything else — here 474.76 against a next-best 283, a 1.7x gap. So the floor lands not at the edge of relevance but in the MIDDLE OF A DENSE BAND: ranks 2 through 11 span 283 to 235, all within 20% of each other. `.take(3)` then selects three members of what is effectively a nine-way tie, and ranks 4 and 5 are separated by 0.006 — six thousandths of a point on a 245-point score. WHICH near-duplicate the caller is shown is therefore decided by scoring noise, not by relevance, whenever the band is crowded. On a 5,000-node design a crowded band is the normal case, not the exception.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is not the guard being lexical rather than semantic: the node DID clear the floor on wording alone, so that candidate was tested and refuted. It is not `related_to` suppressing the block either — reading capture.rs, `related_to` suppresses only the exploratory RELATEDNESS REFUSAL; the `search_first` block is attached whenever `near_matches` is non-empty, independent of it.

⚠️ WHAT COULD NOT BE ESTABLISHED, stated so nobody reads this as tighter than it is. The design has moved since the capture: two of the nodes now scoring above the missed one did not exist at that moment, and the new node's own body has since gained an addendum, which changes its self-score and therefore the floor. So the exact rank at the moment of the write is NOT recoverable, and it is possible the node fell below the floor then rather than being cut by the limit. The CLASS statement does not depend on which: the floor sits inside a near-tie and three are taken from it, so a genuine near-duplicate outside the top three is invisible either way.

NO CAUSES EDGE IS DRAWN: the cause is two constants in the same artifact this finding hangs on, so an edge would point the file at itself and say nothing a reader cannot see here.

NOT A FIX RECOMMENDATION. Raising `NEAR_MATCH_LIMIT` trades a miss for noise, and a band this flat may mean the SCORE is the wrong instrument for this question rather than the cut being in the wrong place. Both are the owner's call.

═══ 2026-09-22 — THE NUMBER MOVED, THE SHAPE DID NOT, AND THIS STAYS OPEN ═══

`NEAR_MATCH_LIMIT` is now 6 (merged #561, green). So "three of a nine-way tie" is out of date as an INSTANCE.

🛑 THE CLASS IS UNCHANGED AND THE CHANGE EVENT SAYS SO ITSELF — it is recorded as `repair: contained_symptom`, not a correction: the floor is still half the new node's own score, a node scored against its own text still sits structurally far above every other hit, so the cut still lands inside a dense band and any fixed limit still takes an arbitrary slice of a near-tie. An eleventh close node is still invisible.

⭐ AND THE SAME DAY PRODUCED EVIDENCE THAT RAISING IT DOES NOT REACH THE REAL COST. `fact:the-brainstorms-only-search-was-the-write-guard-and-it-returned-only-nodes-the-session-had-just-written`: in a long session the guard returned ONLY nodes that session had written minutes earlier, because they share the query's exact phrasing and outrank older nodes written in the design's own vocabulary. Six slots instead of three does not fix that — the agent's own fresh output still fills them.

⇒ NOT CLOSED. `valid_to` would claim the whole thing stopped being true; only the constant did.
